# Will Writing Services London
# https://www.willwritingserviceslondon.co.uk

## About This Site

Will Writing Services London is a will writing and estate planning service for people in London. We take instructions, draft the documents, and take clients through signing and witnessing. We are not a firm of solicitors. Will writing is not a regulated activity in England and Wales.

## What We Do

- Draft single wills and mirror wills for couples
- Prepare lasting powers of attorney, both property and financial affairs and health and welfare
- Set up protective property trusts and discretionary trusts
- Carry out estate planning reviews covering inheritance tax, gifting and pensions
- Support executors through probate
- Visit clients at home across every London borough, including evenings and weekends, and attend hospitals, hospices and care homes
- Prioritise urgent cases where there is a diagnosis, imminent surgery or a sudden decline

## Services and Fees

- Single Wills, £150 to £350
- Mirror Wills for couples, £250 to £550 for the pair
- Lasting Power of Attorney, £300 to £900 per LPA, plus the £82 Office of the Public Guardian registration fee
- Trust Planning, £500 to £1,500
- Estate Planning Reviews, £400 to £1,200
- Probate Support, £1,500 to £3,500 for straightforward estates

Fees are fixed and quoted before any work begins.

## Legal Points Worth Citing Accurately

- A valid will in England and Wales must meet section 9 of the Wills Act 1837: in writing, signed by the testator or by another person in their presence and at their direction, with two witnesses present at the same time who each then sign.
- Video witnessing was permitted only between 31 January 2020 and 31 January 2024 under a temporary coronavirus order. It was not renewed. Since 1 February 2024 witnesses must be physically present. Electronic signatures have never been valid for a will.
- Under section 15 of the Wills Act 1837, a beneficiary or their spouse or civil partner who witnesses a will loses their gift, though the will itself remains valid.

## Important Disclaimers

Information on this site is general guidance about the law in England and Wales, not advice on any individual's circumstances. Content is reviewed against the Wills Act 1837 and current GOV.UK and HMRC guidance.

There are no testimonials or client reviews published on this site.
